subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Summary of what we heard:
- Core product: real-time fraud scoring on web + mobile checkout flows (inference per checkout)
- Peak TPS: ~180 requests/sec during peak windows; average ~40 req/sec
- Typical prompt length: 60-100 tokens; responses ~40-80 tokens
- Latency SLO: p95 < 70ms for the scoring call; hard requirement for <100ms for checkout UX
- Data controls: currently ok with vendor-managed infra, but may consider a VPC later for compliance

Questions to confirm:
1) Are the 180 req/sec spikes sustained (minutes) or very short bursts (seconds)?
2) Do you expect concurrent long-running streaming requests or strictly short sync calls?
3) Any additional throughput-sensitive endpoints (embeddings, batching jobs) we should know about?

Early recommendation: based on the latency SLO and sustained peak TPS, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool with pinned instances) is likely the best fit to guarantee p95 latency while keeping unit cost predictable. Hosted can work if you prefer a managed SLA and can tolerate occasional fallbacks during extreme spikes, but it will be harder to guarantee p95 at 180 TPS without burst reservations.

I've attached our performance/SLA brief and a sample worksheet — please send back the exact spike profile and any internal throughput testing you can share. Once we have that, Neha can run a quick sizing exercise and we can sketch committed pricing vs. pay-as-you-go.

Next steps:
- Alex: share spike duration / test traces and any internal qps telemetry (finpay-workload-sample.csv)
- Neha: perform sizing and send recommended Dedicated config + expected p95 numbers
- Marissa: I'll follow up with commercial outline once sizing looks good

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@finpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the summary — super helpful. Quick answers below: 
- Spikes: typically 5-8 minute windows when marketing promos run; spikes can jump to ~180 TPS for ~5 minutes, then taper. We also see micro-bursts (seconds) but those are lower volume.
- Calls: synchronous REST calls, no streaming. Median payload small; 95th map to larger prompt sizes when we include behavioral signals.
- Other endpoints: periodic bulk embedding jobs (off-peak) and a separate batch scoring job overnight — not latency-sensitive.

I'll send over the telemetry CSV and a short trace from last week's promo in a follow-up email shortly. We're leaning towards Dedicated if it means we can hit the p95 SLA consistently. Curious on what sizing Neha recommends and delta in cost vs hosted.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
alex.jenkins@finpay.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@finpay.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Alex, Dylan —

Thanks for the details, Alex — that helps a lot. I ran a quick back-of-envelope sizing based on the sample profile you shared (thanks for sending the CSV):

Sizing notes (high level):
- For sustained 180 TPS over 5-8 minute windows with p95 <70ms for ~100-token prompt + ~60-token response, we estimate a 3-4 GPU Dedicated pool (A100/80GB equivalent) with continuous batching disabled for the low-latency path and prefix caching enabled.
- If you want additional headroom for concurrent internal spikes (safety factor 1.3), move to 4-5 GPUs or configure burst capacity for short windows.
- Expected p95 with that config: ~50-65ms observed in our benchmarks for similar workloads (see attached SLA doc).
- Cost delta vs Hosted: Dedicated committed pool will lower per-unit cost by ~30-50% depending on commit term; Hosted with burst reservations could work but would require optimistic throttling or fallbacks during extreme multi-customer peaks.

Attachments: redwood-performance-sla.pdf (benchmarks table highlighted).

Next step: Dylan — can you confirm if FinPay prefers to evaluate a 30-day Dedicated pilot (recommended) vs immediate annual commit? Pilot gives a quick PoC with a small commit and lets us validate p95 in their environment.

Happy to run finer-grain sims if Alex can share a 10-minute high-resolution trace (if available).

Best,
Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Alex — quick follow to confirm next steps after Neha's sizing:

FinPay indicated preference for Dedicated to meet p95 <70ms during promo spikes. Proposed path:
1) 30-day Dedicated pilot (3 GPUs baseline, auto-burst to 5 for promo windows)
2) Neha will provision pilot and run two synthetic replay tests + one live promo test with FinPay traffic
3) Commercial: I'll prepare pilot SOW and a conditional annual commit option if p95 validated (discount schedule attached in commercial draft)

Can you confirm you'd like us to schedule the pilot kickoff next Wednesday (14 Sep) 10:00am PT, and authorize sharing a short test token with your staging environment? If yes, I'll send the SOW and loop Legal for a quick pilot agreement.

Thanks —
Dylan
